n0002.title: Blinker
n0002.text:
from amaranth import *


class Blinker(Elaboratable):
    """Toggle `blink_out` every half period.

    `period_param` counts input clock cycles, not milliseconds. The Glasgow
    runs its fabric from a 48 MHz clock, so the variable beside this block
    is set to 48000000 for a one second blink.
    """

    def __init__(self, period_param=48_000_000):
        self.half_period = max(int(period_param) // 2, 1)
        self.blink_out = Signal(1)
        self.counter = Signal(range(self.half_period + 1))

    def elaborate(self, platform):
        m = Module()
        with m.If(self.counter == 0):
            m.d.sync += [
                self.counter.eq(self.half_period - 1),
                self.blink_out.eq(~self.blink_out),
            ]
        with m.Else():
            m.d.sync += self.counter.eq(self.counter - 1)
        return m

n0004.title: Blink rate
n0004.text:
async def testbench(ctx, dut):
    """The output goes straight to a pin, so reach into the blinker for it.

    There is no port block at the top of this design -- nothing needs one
    when the signal's destination is an LED -- so `Top` has no `blink_out`
    of its own. The submodule is an attribute, which is what makes its
    internals reachable from a testbench and from a formal spec.
    """
    blink = dut.blinker.blink_out

    await ctx.tick()
    before = ctx.get(blink)

    # a full period here is 48 million cycles, so check only that it holds
    for _ in range(3):
        await ctx.tick()
    assert ctx.get(blink) == before, "flipped far too early"
